input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Reusing the wrapper's statistics dictionary removes statistics isolation between overlapping invocations. The async wrapper introduces the same defect.
- rationale: When two concurrent calls to the same decorated function both fail their first attempt and retry, their retry-controller copies now update the same dictionary. Both increment its attempt_number, producing 3 although each call is only on attempt 2; callbacks reading retry_state.retry_object.statistics therefore receive incorrect statistics. Previously each copy had its own statistics dictionary. Concurrent clearing can also remove counters while another call is updating them.
critique: The finding identifies a single statistics dict shared by overlapping invocations of the decorated function, in both the sync and async wrappers. It describes the same corruption mechanism: shared counters get merged and concurrent clearing wipes another call's state, so readers see wrong statistics. This matches the label's root cause and failure path.
